rationales.message: A pipe wrench has serrated hook and heel jaws for gripping round work. The illustration instead shows smooth opposing jaw faces and a worm adjustment gear.
Slip-joint pliers have two handles and a two-position sliding pivot. The illustrated tool has one handle and an adjustment wheel beneath its jaws.
This is an adjustable wrench. Its smooth parallel jaws and visible worm adjustment gear match the accepted recognition features. The wheel moves one jaw to change the opening.
Tongue-and-groove pliers have a multi-position adjustment channel and offset serrated jaws. That channel and the pliers linkage are absent from this single-handled wrench.

claims.text: Adjustable wrench is recognized by smooth parallel jaws and visible worm gear for jaw adjustment.
claims.caveat: Recognition cues describe the accepted original illustration and do not imply a universal product silhouette.

claims.text: Pipe wrench is recognized by serrated offset hook and heel jaws and long adjustable body.
claims.caveat: Recognition cues describe the accepted original illustration and do not imply a universal product silhouette.

claims.text: Slip-joint pliers is recognized by two-position sliding pivot and general-purpose gripping jaws.
claims.caveat: Recognition cues describe the accepted original illustration and do not imply a universal product silhouette.

claims.text: Tongue-and-groove pliers is recognized by multi-position tongue-and-groove channel and offset serrated jaws.
